A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Multi-Fidelity Policy Gradient Algorithms. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original robotics simulation results, including learning curves, gradient-estimator variance measurements, and a sampling ablation in Figures 2–7 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulation results, variance measurements, and ablation reported in Section 4, Figures 2–7, and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The new supplementary Algorithm 2 summarizes the MFPG procedure already described in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The correlated sampling, control-variate estimator, REINFORCE/PPO objectives, and critic training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CartPole, InvertedPendulum, Swimmer, Walker2d, Hopper, and HalfCheetah, using the same linearized-dynamics, altered-gravity, and reversed-reward low-fidelity scenarios.

E2.justification: The same single-fidelity REINFORCE, value-subtracted REINFORCE, and PPO comparisons remain. The low-fidelity-only comparator in Figure 6 is also retained.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Tables 3–4 retain the same batch sizes, training budgets, sample ratios, episode and rollout horizons, and evaluation procedures. Algorithm 2 does not establish any experimental setting change.

E4.justification: The variance analysis, reversed-reward mismatch test, policy-reparameterization ablation, and gravity comparisons in Sections 4.1 and 4.4–4.6 are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions specify six random seeds and the same 18-checkpoint, 200-batch variance-estimation procedure. Uncertainty displays and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–7 and Tables 1–2 retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports identical Hopper MFPG-REINFORCE rewards at 1M steps with 90% gravity: 906.36 without value subtraction and 916.40 with it.

T1.justification: The MDP assumptions, joint probability-space construction, control-variate identities, and coefficient formulas are retained. Algorithm 2 restates existing mathematics without adding a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental claims C1–C5, and conclusion retain the same claims about variance reduction, reward improvements, sample efficiency, and effectiveness under fidelity mismatches.

C2.justification: The interpretations of variance reduction, negative reward correlation, and correlated sampling remain unchanged. Section 4.6 retains the qualification that shortened low-fidelity rollouts may introduce estimator bias.

D1.justification: Supplementary Algorithm 2 adds explicit training-loop pseudocode, identifying the sample sets used for coefficient and mean estimation and the high-fidelity-step stopping condition. This clarifies procedural documentation; existing hyperparameters, implementation choices, and the planned code-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning against prior control-variate and multi-fidelity RL research are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Complete MFPG Algorithm supplementary subsection, a short explanatory paragraph, and a cross-reference from Section 3. The remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the Algorithm 2 display, reflows the coefficient discussion, and moves the supplementary hyperparameter tables onto later pages. The cross-reference also causes limited main-text reflow; existing figures and table designs are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 2 collects the previously dispersed sampling, estimation, and optimization steps into one accessible training loop linked from Section 3. This modestly improves clarity and implementation guidance, while the scientific claims, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
